question: A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician because of paresthesias and weakness in her left leg for one year. Her symptoms have become progressively worse during this period and have led to some difficulty walking for the past month. She has had frequent headaches for the past 4 months. She has a history of hypertension and hypothyroidism. Current medications include amlodipine and levothyroxine. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Neurologic examination shows decreased muscle strength in the left lower extremity. Deep tendon reflexes of the lower extremity are 4+ on the left and 2+ on the right side. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of electrolytes, glucose, creatinine, and calcium are within the reference ranges. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypertension and hypothyroidism -> Increased risk of vascular events -> Possible cerebral vascular accident (CVA) -> 70% CHAIN: Paresthesias and weakness in left leg -> Neurologic symptoms -> Brain pathology -> 80% CHAIN: Neurologic examination findings -> Asymmetric muscle strength and reflexes -> Possible brain lesion -> 75% CHAIN: MRI findings -> Presence of brain lesion -> Need for tissue diagnosis -> 85% CHAIN: Need for tissue diagnosis -> Stereotactic brain biopsy -> 70%
analysis: The patient presents with progressive paresthesias and weakness in the left leg, along with frequent headaches. Neurologic examination reveals decreased muscle strength in the left lower extremity and abnormal deep tendon reflexes. The MRI of the brain is likely to show a lesion causing these symptoms. Given the clinical presentation and imaging findings, the most appropriate next step in management would be stereotactic brain biopsy to obtain tissue for histopathological diagnosis.
